> **Library question:** Does this agreement use GH Real Estate as Landlord and the identified dwelling without a nonstandard party or premises structure?

#### 1.1. Parties

This Residential Lease Agreement (the "Lease") is entered into by and between GH Real Estate, LLC, a Kansas limited liability company ("Landlord"), and the individual Tenant(s) named on the cover page and signature page (individually and collectively, "Tenant").

##### 1.2. Premises

Landlord leases to Tenant, and Tenant leases from Landlord, the residential apartment located at ____________________________________________, together with the fixtures, Landlord-provided appliances, assigned keys/access devices, any approved storage unit, and permitted common-area rights described in this Lease or a signed addendum (the "Premises").

### RLA-020 — Occupancy, Responsibility, and Application Accuracy

- **Clause type:** Use, Occupancy and Conduct
- **Source sections:** `1.5`, `1.6`, `1.7`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-020-occupancy-responsibility-and-application-accuracy.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-020-occupancy-responsibility-and-application-accuracy.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the named tenants, approved occupants, joint-responsibility terms, and application-information duties match the source facts?

#### 1.5. Approved Occupants

Occupancy is limited to the named Tenant(s), approved occupants listed below, and children born to or legally placed with a named Tenant during the Lease term, subject to applicable law and lawful occupancy limits. No other person may reside at the Premises without Landlord's prior written approval.

Approved Occupant: ____________________________ Approved Occupant: ____________________________ Approved Occupant: ____________________________

##### 1.6. Joint and Several Responsibility

Each Tenant is jointly and severally responsible for the full amount of Base Rent, Other Charges, actual damages, utilities, lawful fees, reimbursements, and every other lawful obligation under this Lease, regardless of any private arrangement between Tenants. Operational communications to one Tenant may be copied to the other Tenants. Nothing in this section makes statutory service on one Tenant effective service on another person when applicable law requires separate service or delivery.

##### 1.7. Application Accuracy and Contact Information

Tenant represents that all material application, screening, identity, income, occupant, pet, vehicle, and emergency-contact information provided to Landlord was true and complete when provided. A material false statement or omission on which Landlord reasonably relied may constitute a material breach, subject to applicable law. Tenant must update mailing address, phone, email, approved occupants, animals, and vehicles within ten (10) days after a material change.

- **Clause type:** Compliance and Disclosures
- **Source sections:** `1.8`

- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does the standard fair-housing and individualized accommodation-request process apply without attorney-approved alternate language?

#### 1.8. Fair Housing and Accommodation Requests

Landlord conducts housing activities in accordance with applicable federal, Kansas, and Overland Park fair housing laws. An applicant, Tenant, or a person acting on that individual's behalf may request a reasonable accommodation or reasonable modification orally or in writing and need not use a particular form or special words. Landlord will respond promptly and conduct an individualized review. If the disability or disability-related need is not readily apparent, Landlord may request only reliable information reasonably necessary to evaluate the request and will not require detailed medical records or information prohibited by law. No person will be retaliated against for making a good-faith request or exercising a protected right.

## Article 2 — Term, Possession, Renewal, Early Termination, and Holdover

### RLA-040 — Lease Term, Move-In, and Delay of Possession

- **Clause type:** Parties, Premises and Term
- **Source sections:** `2.1`, `2.2`, `2.3`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-040-lease-term-move-in-and-delay-of-possession.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-040-lease-term-move-in-and-delay-of-possession.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the fixed term, move-in conditions, and lawful delay-of-possession remedies apply to this tenancy?

#### 2.1. Lease Term

The Lease begins on __________________ and ends at __________________ on __________________, unless terminated earlier or extended under this Lease or applicable law.

##### 2.2. Move-In and Possession

Tenant may not take possession, receive keys/access devices, or move personal property into the Premises until all amounts due before occupancy are paid in certified or cleared funds, required utilities are established where applicable, all required addenda are signed, and Landlord has delivered possession. Tenant acknowledges that Landlord strongly recommends renter's insurance, but renter's insurance is not required as a condition of possession unless a separate written amendment or addendum signed by Landlord and Tenant states otherwise.

##### 2.3. Delay of Possession

If Landlord fails to deliver possession as required by this Lease, K.S.A. 58-2552, and applicable habitability law, Base Rent abates until possession is delivered. Tenant may, upon at least five (5) days' written notice, terminate this Lease, in which event Landlord shall return the entire Security Deposit and all unearned prepaid Base Rent. Alternatively, Tenant may demand performance and pursue possession and damages as permitted by K.S.A. 58-2560. Nothing in this section limits remedies available when a failure to deliver possession is willful and not in good faith.

---

### RLA-050 — Renewal, Move-Out Notice, and Month-to-Month Terms

- **Clause type:** Parties, Premises and Term
- **Source sections:** `2.4`, `2.5`, `2.6`, `2.7`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-050-renewal-move-out-notice-and-month-to-month-terms.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-050-renewal-move-out-notice-and-month-to-month-terms.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard fixed-term expiration, move-out notice, month-to-month conversion, and renewal rules apply?

#### 2.4. End of Fixed Term and Month-to-Month Conversion

Unless the parties sign a written renewal, Landlord gives nonrenewal notice, Tenant gives required move-out notice, or termination occurs under this Lease or applicable law, occupancy after the fixed term with Landlord's consent will convert to a month-to-month tenancy on the same terms, except as changed by lawful written notice.

##### 2.5. Notice of Move-Out at End of Fixed Term

Tenant must give Landlord at least sixty (60) days' written notice before the Lease end date if Tenant intends to vacate at the end of the fixed term. This notice requirement does not release Tenant from liability for the full fixed term and does not limit either party's statutory termination rights.

##### 2.6. Month-to-Month Termination

Either party may terminate a month-to-month tenancy only by written notice as required by Kansas law. The notice must state that the tenancy terminates on a periodic rent-paying date not less than thirty (30) days after receipt of the notice, unless a different notice period is required by law.

##### 2.7. Rent Increases and Renewal Terms

Rent will not increase during the fixed term unless Tenant agrees in a signed written amendment or unless a specific charge is authorized by this Lease. Any renewal, extension, or month-to-month tenancy may be subject to increased rent or modified terms after lawful written notice. No material change to Rent, Security Deposit, utilities, fees, or lease term is effective during a fixed term unless signed by Landlord and all adult Tenants or otherwise allowed by law.

### RLA-060 — Early Termination and Unauthorized Move-Out

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `2.8`, `2.9`, `2.10`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-060-early-termination-and-unauthorized-move-out.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-060-early-termination-and-unauthorized-move-out.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Will any early termination use a signed buy-out or another lawful basis rather than an automatic personal-circumstances release?

#### 2.8. Tenant Early Termination / Buy-Out

An early-termination buy-out is effective only if Landlord accepts Tenant's request in a separate written agreement signed by Landlord and all Tenants. Unless that agreement provides otherwise, Tenant shall pay Base Rent through the agreed surrender date and a buy-out fee equal to two (2) months' Base Rent. Upon timely surrender and full performance of the agreement, the buy-out fee releases Tenant from Base Rent and re-letting damages accruing after the agreed termination date.

The buy-out does not release amounts accrued before surrender, physical damage, utilities, lawful Other Charges, or another obligation expressly excluded in the signed agreement. Landlord shall not recover duplicate Base Rent, vacancy damages, or re-letting damages for a period compensated by the buy-out fee. If no signed buy-out agreement exists, Section 2.9 and applicable mitigation law control.

##### 2.9. Unauthorized Early Move-Out

If Tenant vacates early without legal excuse or Landlord's written approval, Tenant remains responsible for unpaid Rent, lawful charges, actual damages, reasonable re-letting costs, and any rent deficiency after Landlord makes reasonable efforts to re-rent the Premises, subject to applicable law and without double recovery.

##### 2.10. Job Relocation and Personal Circumstances

A job relocation, school transfer, marriage, divorce, separation, reconciliation, health issue, loss of employment, roommate dispute, or financial hardship does not automatically release Tenant from this Lease unless Landlord approves a written early termination request or applicable law requires release.

### RLA-070 — Military, Protected-Person, and Sole-Tenant Rights

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `2.11`, `2.12`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-070-military-protected-person-and-sole-tenant-rights.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-070-military-protected-person-and-sole-tenant-rights.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the mandatory military, protected-person, casualty, and sole-tenant-death protections apply without restriction?

#### 2.11. Military and Protected-Person Rights

Nothing in this Lease limits any mandatory termination or other right under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act; K.S.A. 58-25,137 protections for persons affected by domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, or stalking; casualty or condemnation law; fair housing law; or another applicable law. A qualifying protected person who provides the statement and any documentation lawfully requested is not liable for Base Rent for the period after vacating as provided by K.S.A. 58-25,137, but remains responsible for amounts lawfully owed for the period before vacating.

Landlord may impose only a reasonable protected-person termination fee, not exceeding one (1) month's Base Rent, and only to the extent permitted by K.S.A. 58-25,137(e). That fee replaces, and is not added to, the Section 2.8 buy-out fee. Termination by a protected person does not automatically terminate the Lease obligations of remaining Tenants unless applicable law requires otherwise.

##### 2.12. Death of Sole Tenant

If the sole Tenant dies, Landlord will communicate with Tenant's lawful representative, estate, or other person legally authorized to act for Tenant. The estate remains responsible for Rent and lawful charges through the termination or surrender date, subject to applicable law. Personal property left behind will be handled under the abandoned-property provisions of this Lease and Kansas law. An emergency contact does not become a tenant merely by being listed as an emergency contact.

### RLA-080 — Holdover

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `2.13`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-080-holdover.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-080-holdover.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does the standard Kansas holdover provision apply without a separately signed holdover arrangement?

#### 2.13. Holdover

If Tenant or any occupant remains in possession after the Lease expires or terminates without Landlord's written consent, Tenant is a holdover occupant and Landlord may bring an action for possession. Unless Landlord gives written consent to a different arrangement, Tenant owes use-and-occupancy charges at the then-current Rent rate, prorated daily, plus lawful actual damages. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, Landlord may recover the maximum holdover damages allowed by Kansas law, including up to one and one-half (1.5) months' periodic Rent or up to one and one-half (1.5) times actual damages, whichever is greater, if awarded or allowed by law. Acceptance of payment does not create a new fixed-term lease unless Landlord agrees in writing.

### RLA-100 — Payment Methods and Receipt

- **Clause type:** Rent, Fees and Payment
- **Source sections:** `3.3`, `3.4`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-100-payment-methods-and-receipt.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-100-payment-methods-and-receipt.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the listed payment methods and provisional electronic-payment timing rules apply?

#### 3.3. Approved Payment Methods

Approved methods are the Online Tenant Portal ACH method, personal check, cashier's check, money order, or another documented method Landlord approves. Cash is not accepted unless Landlord agrees otherwise in writing or applicable law requires acceptance. Landlord may restrict personal checks after a returned payment. If the portal is unavailable, or if Tenant needs another method because of disability, lack of effective electronic access, or another circumstance protected by law, Landlord will provide a reasonable noncash alternative. At least one method will remain available that does not require recurring preauthorized electronic debits.

##### 3.4. Time of Receipt

A payment is received when credited to Landlord's designated account or payment system. An approved ACH or portal payment initiated before the applicable deadline is provisionally timely while legitimately processing if it later completes. If it fails for a reason attributable to Tenant, Tenant's bank, or inaccurate information supplied by Tenant, the unpaid amount is treated as unpaid as of the original due date. No late fee or returned-payment fee will be imposed solely because of an error attributable to Landlord or the payment processor when Tenant timely initiated the payment, supplied accurate information, maintained sufficient available funds, and promptly completes payment by an approved alternative after notice.

### RLA-110 — Late Fees, Delinquent Interest, and Returned Payments

- **Clause type:** Rent, Fees and Payment
- **Source sections:** `3.5`, `3.6`, `3.7`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-110-late-fees-delinquent-interest-and-returned-payments.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-110-late-fees-delinquent-interest-and-returned-payments.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Are the stated late-fee, simple-interest, and returned-payment provisions approved for this lease without an attorney-approved exception?

#### 3.5. Late Fees

If any portion of monthly Base Rent remains unpaid after 5:00 p.m. Central Time on the 5th day of the month, Tenant shall be charged a late fee equal to five percent (5%) of the unpaid monthly Base Rent. If any portion of monthly Base Rent remains unpaid after 5:00 p.m. Central Time on the 10th day of the month, Tenant shall be charged an additional late fee equal to five percent (5%) of the unpaid monthly Base Rent. Total late fees for a monthly Base Rent charge shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the unpaid monthly Base Rent for that month. Late fees are intended to compensate Landlord for administrative time, inconvenience, collection administration, and loss caused by late payment, and are not interest. Late fees are not charged on prior late fees, interest, returned-payment fees, online payment or processing fees, administrative fees, application fees, utility reimbursements, repair charges, security deposits, court costs, collection costs, or other fee-only or reimbursement charges. No late fee is charged solely because an approved ACH or portal payment is pending, if that payment was initiated before the applicable deadline and later completes; if the payment fails, late fees may apply as of the original due date.

##### 3.6. Interest on Delinquent Rent

If unpaid Base Rent remains unpaid after the thirtieth (30th) calendar day following its original due date, Landlord may assess simple interest on the unpaid Base Rent only at ten percent (10%) per year, or the maximum lawful rate if lower, accruing prospectively beginning on the thirty-first (31st) day until paid. Interest is calculated daily, is not compounded, and may be billed no more often than once per calendar month.

No interest is charged on prior interest, late fees, returned-payment fees, payment-processing fees, pet charges, storage rent, utility reimbursements, repair charges, deposits, court costs, collection costs, or other fee-only or reimbursement charges.

##### 3.7. Returned Payments

If a payment fails because of insufficient funds, a stop-payment instruction, an invalid or closed account, revocation, inaccurate information supplied by Tenant, or another reason attributable to Tenant or Tenant's financial institution, Tenant owes one returned-payment fee of $30.00, or the maximum lawful amount if lower. No returned-payment fee is imposed for a duplicate attempt, a valid unauthorized-transfer claim, or a failure caused by Landlord, the payment provider, or a system error not attributable to Tenant. Any returned-payment fee will be separately invoiced and will not be electronically debited unless separately authorized and after any notice required by law.

### RLA-120 — Application of Payments and Other Charges

- **Clause type:** Rent, Fees and Payment

- **Source JSON:** [`rla-120-application-of-payments-and-other-charges.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-120-application-of-payments-and-other-charges.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Will payments and documented non-rent charges be handled under the stated order and pass-through limits?

#### 3.8. Application of Payments

Unless applicable law, a court order, or a contemporaneous written agreement requires otherwise, payments will be applied first to current Base Rent, then to the oldest unpaid Base Rent, and then to other lawful charges in chronological order. Acceptance of a partial or late payment has the effect provided by K.S.A. 58-2566.

##### 3.9. Other Charges

Other Charges means lawful amounts owed under this Lease other than the Security Deposit and Base Rent, including utility reimbursements, storage rent, pet rent, documented repair costs caused by Tenant, and documented HOA or municipal charges caused by Tenant or persons or animals for whom Tenant is responsible. Other Charges are due within ten (10) days after written demand unless this Lease states another due date. Labeling an amount an Other Charge does not make it Base Rent or authorize a nonpayment eviction remedy that applicable law does not allow.

##### 3.10. Government, HOA, Utility, and Tax-Related Charges

Tenant is responsible only for an actual, documented charge directly caused by a proven act or omission of Tenant, an occupant, guest, invitee, ordinary pet, assistance animal, or Tenant's property. Tenant is not responsible under this section for Landlord's ordinary property taxes, ownership assessments, licensing expenses, capital expenses, or code violations not caused by Tenant. Landlord will provide reasonable supporting documentation and will not add a markup unless expressly stated and lawful.

### RLA-130 — Withholding, Late Payment, Statements, and Credits

- **Clause type:** Rent, Fees and Payment
- **Source sections:** `3.11`, `3.12`, `3.13`, `3.14`

- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

#### 3.11. No Withholding or Offset Except as Allowed by Law

Tenant must pay Rent in full when due and may not withhold, offset, or deduct Rent except as expressly allowed by applicable law. Nothing in this Lease waives Tenant's non-waivable rights or remedies under Kansas law.

##### 3.12. No Excuse for Late Payment

Job loss, reduced hours, health issues, travel, payment-processor issues, roommate disputes, or financial hardship do not excuse late payment. Tenant should contact Landlord before default if a payment issue arises, but Landlord is not required to accept late or partial payment.

##### 3.13. Monthly Statements and Invoices

Any monthly statement, invoice, ledger, or portal balance is provided for convenience and collection administration. It does not amend this Lease. If a monthly statement or invoice conflicts with this Lease, this Lease controls unless a signed written amendment states otherwise.

##### 3.14. Concessions and Credits

Any move-in concession, discount, waived fee, free-rent period, or other credit must be in writing. If Tenant defaults, moves out early without legal excuse, or fails to satisfy the conditions stated for the concession, Landlord may revoke only those concessions that the written concession agreement expressly states are conditional, to the extent allowed by law.

- **Clause type:** Rent, Fees and Payment

### RLA-150 — Deposit Amount and Kansas Caps

- **Clause type:** Deposits and Prepaid Amounts

> **Library question:** Will the governed deposit amount satisfy the furnished-unit and ordinary-pet limits after ownership and cap validation?

#### 4.1. Security Deposit Amount

Tenant shall pay a Security Deposit of $__________________. The Security Deposit is not advance rent and may not be used by Tenant as last month's rent or to offset Rent or other amounts due.

##### 4.2. Kansas Deposit Caps

For an unfurnished dwelling unit, the Security Deposit shall not exceed one month's periodic rent. If the dwelling unit is furnished, the Security Deposit shall not exceed one and one-half months' periodic rent. If Landlord permits Tenant to keep a pet, Landlord may require an additional refundable pet security deposit up to one-half month's rent, subject to Kansas law. Assistance animals are addressed separately in the Pets and Assistance Animals section.

### RLA-160 — Deposit Application, Return, and Multiple Tenants

- **Clause type:** Deposits and Prepaid Amounts
- **Source sections:** `4.3`, `4.4`, `4.5`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-160-deposit-application-return-and-multiple-tenants.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-160-deposit-application-return-and-multiple-tenants.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard lawful-deduction, accounting, return, and multiple-tenant refund rules apply?

#### 4.3. Application of Security Deposit

Upon termination of the tenancy, Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to accrued rent, damages beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning or restoration beyond ordinary wear and tear, unpaid utilities, unpaid lawful charges, missing keys or access devices, pet-related damage, storage-unit damage, and other legally allowable charges under this Lease and Kansas law.

##### 4.4. Return and Itemization

Landlord shall provide a written itemization of every deduction, including accrued Base Rent, and return the remaining Security Deposit within fourteen (14) days after determining the amount of expenses, damages, or other lawful charges, but no later than thirty (30) days after termination of the tenancy and delivery of possession. Landlord will mail the accounting and refund to Tenant's written forwarding address. If no forwarding address is provided, Landlord shall mail them to Tenant's last known address. As a contractual practice, Landlord will provide the accounting within this period without requiring a separate demand from Tenant.

##### 4.5. Multiple Tenants

Unless all Tenants provide written instructions signed by all adult Tenants, Landlord may issue any deposit refund and accounting jointly to all Tenants and mail it to the forwarding address provided by any one Tenant or to the last known address.

#### 4.6. No Security Deposit as Rent

Tenant may not apply the Security Deposit to Rent or use it as last month's rent. Attempting to do so is a material breach and does not excuse the rent obligation. To the extent allowed by Kansas law and this Lease, misuse of the Security Deposit as Rent may result in forfeiture of the Security Deposit while preserving Landlord's right to recover unpaid Rent.

##### 4.7. No Automatic Forfeiture for Ordinary Violations

Except as expressly allowed by Kansas law for improper application of the Security Deposit to Rent, the Security Deposit is not automatically forfeited because of a Lease violation. Landlord may apply it only to amounts lawfully deductible. If lawful deductions exceed the Security Deposit, Tenant remains responsible for the balance.

##### 4.8. Non-Refundable Fees

A non-refundable fee is enforceable only if separately stated, clearly labeled, and not held to secure future damage, rent, or other performance. Any amount that functions as security is part of the Security Deposit and is subject to Kansas deposit limits and accounting requirements regardless of its label.

If ownership or management changes, the Security Deposit will be transferred or otherwise handled as required by law, and Tenant will receive any notice required by law. No transfer, notice, or Lease provision releases any person from deposit liability that Kansas law preserves, including liability under K.S.A. 58-2550(f) and 58-2554.

> **Library question:** Are all tenant-assigned utility accounts expressly identified, with the standard cooperation duties applying?

#### 5.2. Failure to Maintain Utilities

Failure to maintain a utility expressly assigned to Tenant may constitute a material breach only if it creates a material health, safety, habitability, freeze, plumbing, pest, mold, or property-damage risk and after any notice and cure required by law. If Landlord pays a utility charge that Tenant is responsible for, Tenant must reimburse the reasonable, actual, documented amount as an Other Charge after written demand. This section does not excuse Landlord's non-waivable duties or authorize utility interruption as self-help.

##### 5.3. Proof and Account Cooperation

Tenant must provide proof of utility account setup upon Landlord's reasonable request and must cooperate with Landlord, HOA, and utility providers to prevent interruption, leaks, waste, meter problems, or service issues.

### RLA-200 — Trash, Recycling, and Bulk Items

- **Clause type:** Utilities and Services
- **Source sections:** `5.4`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-200-trash-recycling-and-bulk-items.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-200-trash-recycling-and-bulk-items.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does the property use the standard trash, recycling, container, and bulk-item rules?

#### 5.4. Trash, Recycling, and Bulk Items

Tenant must place trash and recycling only in approved receptacles and must comply with city, HOA, and hauler rules. Trash and recycling containers must be stored in a screened or enclosed location except for scheduled pickup, may not be placed out earlier than allowed by city or HOA rules, and must be removed promptly after collection. Tenant must bag trash, flatten cardboard as required, keep containers accessible to the hauler, and arrange bulk-item pickup only as allowed by the HOA and hauler. Trash, garbage, food waste, furniture, mattresses, construction debris, hazardous waste, and bulk items may not be stored in common areas, patios, balconies, stairways, hallways, yards, or outside the Premises except as allowed for scheduled pickup. Tenant is responsible for charges caused by improper disposal.

### RLA-210 — Plumbing, Freeze, and Outdoor Water

#### 5.5. Plumbing Rules

Tenant may not place grease, oils, wipes, paper towels, feminine products, diapers, toys, rags, food scraps, cat litter, chemicals, drain cleaner, or other improper items into drains, toilets, disposals, sinks, or plumbing. Tenant must promptly report leaks, slow drains, running toilets, backups, low heat, or freeze risks. Tenant may use a plunger for ordinary clogs but may not use chemical drain cleaners or perform unauthorized plumbing work.

##### 5.6. Plumbing and Freeze Damage

Tenant is responsible for plumbing stoppages, overflow, freeze damage, water damage, and related costs caused or worsened by Tenant, occupants, guests, pets, improper items, misuse, failure to maintain utilities, failure to keep heat on, or failure to report issues promptly.

##### 5.7. Outdoor Water Spigots

Tenant must disconnect hoses from outdoor spigots during freezing weather and must not leave hoses, sprinklers, or water devices running unattended. Tenant is responsible for damage caused by misuse or failure to follow seasonal instructions.

#### 5.8. Utility Interruptions

Landlord is not an insurer against interruptions caused by a utility provider, storm, outage, government action, Tenant nonpayment, or circumstances outside Landlord's reasonable control. Tenant must promptly report any condition affecting health, safety, or property. This section does not excuse a duty imposed by K.S.A. 58-2553 or liability for an interruption caused or prolonged by Landlord's breach, negligence, or willful conduct.

## Article 6 — Maintenance, Repairs, Mold, Pest Control, and Environmental Hazards

### RLA-230 — Maintenance Responsibilities and Requests

- **Clause type:** Maintenance, Repairs and Condition
- **Source sections:** `6.1`, `6.2`, `6.3`, `6.4`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-230-maintenance-responsibilities-and-requests.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-230-maintenance-responsibilities-and-requests.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard landlord and tenant maintenance duties, request channels, emergency reporting, and repair-access rules apply?

#### 6.1. Landlord Maintenance Responsibilities

Landlord shall comply with applicable building and housing codes materially affecting health and safety; exercise reasonable care in maintaining common areas; maintain Landlord-supplied electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning systems in good and safe working order; provide and arrange removal of appropriate common waste receptacles; and supply running water, reasonable hot water, and reasonable heat except where a lawful direct utility arrangement places generation and payment within Tenant's exclusive control. Nothing in this Lease delegates or waives a duty that K.S.A. 58-2549, 58-2553, or another law makes nondelegable.

##### 6.2. Tenant Maintenance Responsibilities

Tenant shall perform the duties imposed by K.S.A. 58-2555, including keeping the occupied area as clean and safe as its condition permits, removing waste safely, using facilities and appliances reasonably, avoiding damage, and not disturbing other residents' peaceful enjoyment. Tenant shall replace ordinary consumables such as light bulbs and filters only if expressly assigned. No Tenant duty or later rule shifts a Landlord duty that may be delegated only through a separate signed agreement, good faith, adequate consideration, or other requirements of K.S.A. 58-2553.

##### 6.3. Maintenance Requests and Emergencies

Routine maintenance requests may be submitted through the tenant portal, email, text, or another method Landlord reasonably approves. A portal request does not prevent Tenant from giving any separate statutory notice in a method permitted by law. Emergencies involving fire, flood, active leak, gas odor, electrical hazard, dangerous loss of heat, sewer backup, or immediate threat to life or severe property damage must be reported immediately by phone after calling 911 or the utility provider where appropriate.

##### 6.4. Access for Repairs and Scheduling

Tenant must provide reasonable access for inspections, repairs, contractors, pest treatment, code work, insurance inspections, showings, and other purposes permitted by K.S.A. 58-2557 or applicable law. Tenant must reasonably secure animals and valuables. If Tenant unlawfully refuses access, Landlord may seek the remedies in K.S.A. 58-2571 and recover only reasonable, actual, documented costs or damages to the extent allowed by law.

#### 6.5. Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detectors

Landlord shall supply and install all smoke alarms and carbon-monoxide alarms required by applicable law and shall document that they are present and operational when possession is delivered. After taking possession, Tenant shall test and maintain smoke alarms inside the rental unit as required by K.S.A. 31-162, promptly report any problem, and never disable, remove, obstruct, or tamper with an alarm. Landlord remains responsible for every owner duty imposed by law.

### RLA-250 — Mold and Pest Control

- **Clause type:** Maintenance, Repairs and Condition
- **Source sections:** `6.6`, `6.7`

> **Library question:** Do the standard moisture-prevention, mold-reporting, pest-control, and causation rules apply?

#### 6.6. Mold Prevention and Reporting

Tenant must use reasonable ventilation, temperature control, cleaning, and moisture prevention and must promptly report leaks, condensation, water intrusion, dampness, visible mold, mildew, or musty odors. Tenant may be charged only for reasonable, documented costs to the extent reliable evidence establishes that Tenant caused or materially worsened the condition. Tenant is not responsible for a preexisting condition, structural defect, common-area source, or Landlord's failure to perform a non-waivable duty.

##### 6.7. Pest Control and Bed Bugs

Tenant must keep the Premises reasonably clean, promptly report signs of pests, cooperate with lawful inspection and treatment, and not use unsafe self-treatment. Tenant may be charged only for reasonable, documented treatment and related costs to the extent reliable evidence establishes that Tenant, an occupant, guest, animal, poor housekeeping, unreported condition, or infested personal property caused or materially worsened the infestation. Tenant is not responsible for a preexisting infestation, structural defect, common-area source, or Landlord's failure to perform a non-waivable duty.

- **Clause type:** Compliance and Disclosures
- **Source sections:** `6.8`, `6.9`

#### 6.8. Asbestos and Building Materials

Because the property may have been built before 1981, some building materials may contain asbestos or other regulated materials. Tenant may not scrape, sand, drill, cut, disturb, remove, or attach anything to walls, ceilings, flooring, insulation, pipe wrap, texture, tile, or other suspect materials in a manner that may release dust or fibers without Landlord's prior written consent. Tenant must promptly report damaged or deteriorated building materials, ceiling leaks, loose tiles, or similar conditions.

##### 6.9. Lead-Based Paint Renovation Restriction

Because the property was built before 1978 or is being treated as pre-1978 housing for disclosure purposes, Tenant may not scrape, sand, remove, drill, cut, disturb, renovate, repair, or paint surfaces in a manner that may disturb lead-based paint without Landlord's prior written consent. Tenant must report deteriorated paint promptly. Any lead-related work must be handled by Landlord or properly certified professionals as required by law.

If repair, casualty, code work, pest treatment, environmental remediation, or other work not caused by Tenant reasonably requires Tenant to temporarily vacate the Premises, Landlord may arrange temporary relocation or other lawful accommodation as required by law. If the condition or work is caused by Tenant, occupants, guests, pets, or Tenant's property, Tenant is responsible for resulting reasonable costs to the extent allowed by law.

#### 7.1. Provided Appliances

The following items are provided with the Premises unless crossed out or modified in writing: ____________________. These items are provided for Tenant's use and remain Landlord property unless Landlord states otherwise in writing.

##### 7.2. Appliance and Furnishing Responsibility

Tenant must keep provided appliances and furnishings clean and use them only for their intended purposes and according to manufacturer instructions. Landlord is responsible for repair or replacement required by ordinary wear and tear and legal maintenance obligations. Tenant is responsible for repair or replacement required because of misuse, negligence, damage, improper installation, overloading, failure to clean, failure to report a malfunction, or use inconsistent with manufacturer instructions.

##### 7.3. No Warranty of Convenience

Landlord does not guarantee uninterrupted availability of a nonessential amenity, but will use reasonable efforts to repair or replace malfunctioning Landlord-provided appliances. Nothing in this section waives Landlord's duties under K.S.A. 58-2553, applicable code, the Lease, or another law, or limits a remedy that cannot lawfully be waived.

### RLA-290 — Move-In and Move-Out Condition

- **Clause type:** Maintenance, Repairs and Condition
- **Source sections:** `7.4`, `7.5`

> **Library question:** Will the parties complete the statutory move-in inventory and use any move-out inspection only as a preliminary record?

#### 7.4. Move-In Inventory

Within five (5) days after the initial date of occupancy or delivery of possession, Landlord or Landlord's representative and Tenant shall jointly inventory the Premises and complete a written condition record covering the Premises and all Landlord-provided furnishings and appliances. Duplicate copies shall be signed, and Tenant shall receive one signed copy. Photographs and unilateral notes may supplement but do not replace the joint process required by K.S.A. 58-2548.

##### 7.5. Move-Out Inspection

After Tenant vacates and removes personal property, the parties may document move-out condition on a separate record. Tenant may request to attend if scheduling is practical. Move-out observations are preliminary and do not constitute a release, settlement, final damage determination, or Security Deposit accounting. Every deduction remains subject to Section 4 and Kansas law.

### RLA-300 — Alterations, Installations, and Exterior Appearance

- **Clause type:** Maintenance, Repairs and Condition

#### 7.6. Alterations and Installations

Tenant may not make repairs, alterations, painting, flooring changes, lock or fixture changes, plumbing installations, shelves, mounts, cameras, alarm systems, or other modifications without Landlord's prior written consent, except as applicable law provides. Nothing in this section restricts a reasonable accommodation or reasonable modification protected by fair housing law; such a request may be made orally or in writing and will be evaluated under Section 1.8. Tenant is responsible for actual damage and lawful restoration costs from unauthorized work.

##### 7.7. Satellite / Antenna and Legal Exceptions

Any satellite dish, antenna, or similar device is subject to applicable federal law, HOA rules, safety restrictions, and Landlord's reasonable installation requirements. Nothing in this Lease prohibits an installation that Landlord is legally required to allow, but Tenant must request approval before installation and must comply with lawful conditions.

##### 7.8. Window Coverings, Signs, and Exterior Appearance

Window coverings visible from outside must be ordinary curtains, blinds, or shades and must present a neat exterior appearance. Sheets, blankets, foil, cardboard, signs, decals, flags, or other improvised coverings may not be used in windows unless Landlord approves in writing or applicable law requires an exception.

A third-party locksmith's actual charge may be higher and is paid directly by Tenant unless law requires otherwise.

## Article 8 — Landlord Access, Use of Premises, Conduct, Drugs, and Safety

### RLA-330 — Landlord Access and Showings

- **Clause type:** Access and Inspection
- **Source sections:** `8.1`, `8.2`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-330-landlord-access-and-showings.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-330-landlord-access-and-showings.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard Kansas notice, emergency-entry, inspection, repair, and showing rules apply?

#### 8.1. Landlord Access

Landlord may enter at reasonable hours, after reasonable notice, to inspect the Premises; make necessary or agreed repairs, decorations, alterations, or improvements; supply necessary or agreed services; or exhibit the Premises to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workers, or contractors. Except when circumstances reasonably require shorter notice, Landlord ordinarily will give at least twenty-four (24) hours' notice. Landlord shall not abuse the right of access or use it to harass Tenant.

Landlord may enter without Tenant's consent only in an extreme hazard involving potential loss of life or severe property damage, during an extended absence or actual abandonment when K.S.A. 58-2565 authorizes entry, under a court order, or as otherwise expressly authorized by law. Suspicion of abandonment alone does not authorize entry.

##### 8.2. Showings

During the final sixty (60) days of the Lease term, after notice of nonrenewal or move-out, after default, or when the Premises is listed for sale or financing inspection, Tenant must reasonably cooperate with showings to prospective tenants, buyers, lenders, inspectors, contractors, or agents. Landlord will use reasonable efforts to minimize inconvenience.

---

### RLA-340 — Absence, Residential Use, and Guests

- **Clause type:** Use, Occupancy and Conduct
- **Source sections:** `8.3`, `8.4`, `8.5`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-340-absence-residential-use-and-guests.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-340-absence-residential-use-and-guests.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard extended-absence notice, residential-use, and guest-limit provisions fit the tenancy facts?

#### 8.3. Extended Absence

Tenant must notify Landlord in writing of any planned absence from the Premises exceeding seven (7) consecutive days and must take reasonable steps to protect the Premises, including maintaining heat, utilities, plumbing protection, security, and emergency contact availability. Tenant remains responsible for damage caused or worsened by absence or failure to notify.

##### 8.4. Residential Use Only

The Premises may be used only as a private residence by Tenant and approved occupants. Ordinary remote or administrative work is permitted if it involves no employees or customers visiting the property, signage, stored business inventory, unusual deliveries, nuisance, increased traffic, unlawful use, zoning violation, insurance issue, or material increase in property risk. Short-term rental, boarding, lodging, public-facing work, or high-traffic commercial activity requires Landlord's prior written consent and compliance with law, zoning, HOA rules, insurance, and this Lease.

##### 8.5. Guests and Unauthorized Occupants

Guests may not stay more than fourteen (14) consecutive days or twenty-one (21) total days in any six-month period without Landlord's prior written approval. Receiving mail, possessing a temporary key, contributing to expenses, or any single factor does not conclusively establish unauthorized residency; Landlord will consider the total circumstances. Landlord may require screening and a signed Lease amendment before approving a new adult resident. This section is subject to Section 1.8, including requests involving a live-in aide, caregiver, or other protected accommodation.

### RLA-350 — Conduct, Noise, Smoking, and Controlled Substances

- **Clause type:** Use, Occupancy and Conduct
- **Source sections:** `8.6`, `8.7`, `8.8`, `8.9`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-350-conduct-noise-smoking-and-controlled-substances.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-350-conduct-noise-smoking-and-controlled-substances.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard lawful-conduct, quiet-hours, smoking, vaping, and controlled-substance restrictions apply?

#### 8.6. Legal Compliance and Conduct

Tenant, occupants, guests, invitees, and pets must comply with all laws, ordinances, HOA rules, fire codes, health and safety rules, and reasonable written property rules. Tenant must not create nuisance, harassment, threats, disturbance, damage, unsafe conditions, excessive traffic, disorderly conduct, or interference with other residents' quiet enjoyment.

##### 8.7. Noise and Quiet Hours

Noise must be kept at a reasonable level at all times and especially between 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. Tenant is responsible for noise from televisions, speakers, instruments, parties, guests, pets, vehicles, heavy walking, and other sources. Repeated complaints or verified disturbances may constitute a material breach.

##### 8.8. Smoking and Vaping Prohibited

Smoking, vaping, burning incense, and use of cigarettes, cigars, pipes, e-cigarettes, hookahs, marijuana, cannabis, or similar products are prohibited inside the Premises, in common areas, in storage areas, and within twenty (20) feet of the building or any location where smoke or odor may enter the building. Tenant is responsible for smoke, odor, residue, cleaning, repainting, deodorizing, filter replacement, damage, and related costs caused by Tenant, occupants, guests, or invitees.

##### 8.9. Marijuana and Controlled Substances

Tenant, occupants, guests, and invitees may not grow, produce, possess, consume, ingest, smoke, vape, distribute, manufacture, or store marijuana, cannabis, illegal drugs, or drug paraphernalia on or about the Premises, including activities claimed to be medical or recreational, except for lawful prescription medication possessed and used by the person for whom it is prescribed.

### RLA-360 — Fire, Hazardous Materials, and Security

- **Clause type:** Use, Occupancy and Conduct
- **Source sections:** `8.10`, `8.11`, `8.12`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-360-fire-hazardous-materials-and-security.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-360-fire-hazardous-materials-and-security.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does the property use the standard grill, open-flame, hazardous-material, fire-safety, and crime-reporting rules?

#### 8.10. Grills and Open-Flame Devices

Charcoal grills, propane or LP-gas grills, natural-gas grills, pellet or wood-burning grills, smokers, hibachis, fire pits, torches, and other open-flame cooking or heating devices are prohibited on balconies, decks, patios, landings, or within ten (10) feet of combustible construction and in every other location restricted by fire code, HOA rule, insurance, or written property rule. Propane cylinders, lighter fluid, charcoal, pellets, fireworks, and other grilling fuel may not be stored in the Premises, basement, common area, or storage unit.

A listed electric cooking appliance may be used outdoors only in a location Landlord designates in writing, on a stable noncombustible surface, attended continuously, connected without an unsafe extension cord, and operated according to manufacturer instructions, code, HOA rules, and written property rules. No cooking device may be used indoors, in the basement, in a garage, or in another enclosed area. Any open-flame exception requires prior written Landlord approval and site-specific confirmation from the appropriate fire official.

##### 8.11. Hazardous Materials and Fire Safety

Tenant may not store gasoline, kerosene, fuels, explosives, fireworks, flammable liquids, hazardous chemicals, excessive paint or solvent, ammunition, excessive combustibles, or other dangerous materials in or around the Premises except ordinary household products stored safely in ordinary quantities. Tenant must not block exits, stairways, halls, electrical panels, fire extinguishers, mechanical areas, or access routes.

##### 8.12. Security and Crime Reporting

Tenant must exercise reasonable care for personal safety, keep doors and windows secured, protect access devices, and call 911 before contacting Landlord in an emergency. Landlord does not insure Tenant against crime or guarantee that lighting, locks, cameras, or other measures will prevent criminal activity. Nothing in this section exculpates or limits liability imposed by law or waives a non-waivable duty or remedy.

## Article 9 — Pets and Assistance Animals

### RLA-370 — Pet Approval and Charges

- **Clause type:** Animals and Accommodations
- **Source sections:** `9.1`, `9.2`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-370-pet-approval-and-charges.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-370-pet-approval-and-charges.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Is every ordinary pet separately approved and charged only through the governed Ordinary Pet Addendum?

#### 9.1. No Animals Without Approval

An ordinary pet may not be kept, brought, housed, fed, watched, or allowed on the Premises without Landlord's prior written approval. This prior-approval rule does not apply to a service animal, assistance animal, or visiting animal protected by applicable law. A request for an assistance animal may be oral or written and will be evaluated under Sections 1.8 and 9.3.

##### 9.2. Pet Charges and Pet Addendum

If Landlord approves an ordinary pet, Tenant must sign the Ordinary Pet Addendum and pay only the pet charges specifically stated there. Any refundable Pet Security Deposit is part of the statutory Security Deposit regime and may not exceed the aggregate Kansas limit. Ordinary pet rent, fees, deposits, breed limits, weight limits, and number limits do not apply to an assistance animal to the extent prohibited by law.

### RLA-380 — Assistance Animals

- **Clause type:** Animals and Accommodations
- **Source sections:** `9.3`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-380-assistance-animals.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-380-assistance-animals.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does an assistance-animal request require the individualized accommodation process rather than ordinary-pet terms?

#### 9.3. Assistance Animals

An assistance animal allowed as a reasonable accommodation is not an ordinary pet. No pet rent, pet fee, or pet deposit will be charged for a legally protected assistance animal. If the disability or need is not readily apparent, Landlord may request only reliable information allowed by law. A direct-threat, substantial-damage, restriction, or removal decision will be based on an individualized assessment of objective evidence concerning the specific animal's actual conduct and consideration of whether reasonable measures can sufficiently reduce the risk. Tenant remains responsible for actual animal-caused damage and generally applicable sanitation and control duties to the extent allowed by law.

---

### RLA-390 — Animal Damage, Unauthorized Animals, and Compliance

- **Clause type:** Animals and Accommodations
- **Source sections:** `9.4`, `9.5`, `9.6`, `9.7`, `9.8`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-390-animal-damage-unauthorized-animals-and-compliance.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-390-animal-damage-unauthorized-animals-and-compliance.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard animal-damage, unauthorized-animal, licensing, revocation, and wildlife rules apply?

#### 9.4. Pet Damage and Conduct

Tenant is responsible for reasonable, actual, documented costs and damages caused by an approved or unauthorized animal to the extent allowed by law, including damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, odor, stains, waste, pest treatment, injury, and actual HOA or municipal charges. Ordinary pets must be controlled and comply with legally required licensing and vaccination duties and the Ordinary Pet Addendum. Assistance animals are governed by Section 9.3 and any Assistance Animal Accommodation Addendum. Landlord will not recover twice for the same loss.

##### 9.5. Unauthorized Animals

An unauthorized ordinary pet is a material violation. Landlord may require removal, recover actual damages, and impose only ordinary-pet charges expressly stated in a signed agreement and allowed by law. No pet charge or ordinary-pet remedy applies to an animal that must be allowed as a reasonable accommodation when prohibited by law.

##### 9.6. Vaccination, Licensing, and Local Ordinances

Tenant must comply with all animal licensing, vaccination, leash, sanitation, waste, nuisance, and animal-control laws. Dogs must be leashed and under control outside the Premises as required by Overland Park rules and HOA rules. Tenant must promptly provide proof of compliance upon Landlord's reasonable request.

##### 9.7. Revocation of Pet Permission

Permission for an ordinary pet may be revoked only after any notice and cure opportunity required by the Lease and law if Tenant violates the Ordinary Pet Addendum, law, HOA rules, or reasonable property rules, or if the animal creates an unmitigated nuisance, direct threat, repeated disturbance, unsanitary condition, or property damage. Assistance-animal issues are handled through the individualized accommodation process and not under this ordinary-pet revocation provision.

##### 9.8. No Feeding Stray or Wild Animals

Tenant may not feed, harbor, or attract stray animals, wildlife, birds, raccoons, squirrels, cats, or other animals on or near the Premises in a manner that creates pests, nuisance, property damage, or safety concerns.

#### 10.1. Common Areas

Tenant must keep hallways, stairs, laundry areas, sidewalks, entries, yards, parking areas, and other common areas free of trash, storage, bicycles, furniture, packages, obstructions, smoking, and nuisance. An approved ordinary pet or protected assistance animal may use common areas under reasonable control and sanitation rules. Landlord may remove unauthorized property only after notice when practical and in a manner permitted by law, and may recover reasonable, actual, documented costs caused by Tenant.

##### 10.2. Laundry

Laundry facilities, if provided, are for ordinary residential use only. Tenant must clean lint traps, promptly remove laundry, use machines properly, and report malfunctions. Landlord is not responsible for lost, damaged, or stolen laundry unless required by law.

### RLA-410 — Ancillary Storage and Stored Property

- **Clause type:** Ancillary Storage
- **Source sections:** `10.3`, `10.4`

#### 10.3. Storage Units

Storage is allowed only if Landlord approves a specific ancillary storage area in a signed Ancillary Storage Addendum. Storage rent is an Other Charge. No separate storage Security Deposit or contractual lien applies under that form. Tenant must not store flammable, hazardous, illegal, perishable, pest-attracting, high-value, or otherwise prohibited items. Landlord does not insure Tenant's stored property, and no provision exculpates liability imposed by law. If the arrangement is legally classified as self-service storage, this form and process must be replaced before use.

##### 10.4. Property Left in Storage, Common Areas, or Premises

Property left after surrender, actual abandonment, eviction, or move-out, or left in an unauthorized common area, will be handled only under controlling Kansas law, including K.S.A. 58-2565 where applicable. No Lease clause, rule, or storage termination shortens the statutory waiting, notice, mailing, publication, redemption, or disposition process. Tenant may be responsible for reasonable, actual, documented removal, storage, notice, hauling, disposal, cleaning, and repair costs to the extent recoverable by law.

#### 10.5. Building Security

Tenant must not prop open exterior doors, share access codes with unauthorized persons, duplicate keys without permission, tamper with locks, or allow unauthorized access. Lost keys, fobs, codes, or access devices must be reported promptly.

##### 10.6. Exterior Cleanliness, Patios, Balconies, and Storage

Patios, balconies, landings, entries, and exterior areas must be neat and used only for ordinary outdoor furniture and approved plants unless HOA rules or Landlord state otherwise. No indoor furniture, appliances, trash, rugs over railings, laundry, storage boxes, bikes, grills, fuel, tires, tools, construction materials, signs, or unsightly items may be kept outside without written approval.

##### 10.7. Snow and Ice

Landlord retains responsibility for reasonable care of common areas as required by K.S.A. 58-2553. Tenant is responsible only for an exclusive-use area expressly identified here: ______________________________, and only to the extent that assignment is lawful. Tenant must report hazardous conditions and must not create ice hazards by discharging water, draining hoses, or leaving items in walkways. No handbook or later rule shifts a nondelegable common-area duty.

### RLA-430 — Parking and Vehicles

- **Clause type:** Use, Occupancy and Conduct

> **Library question:** Do the source parking allowance and standard towing, vehicle-repair, and vehicle-risk provisions apply?

#### 10.8. Parking

Tenant may use __________________ parking spaces, subject to HOA rules and availability. No specific stall is assigned or guaranteed unless Landlord states otherwise in writing. Vehicles must be operable, licensed, insured, and lawfully parked. Tenant and guests may not block driveways, dumpsters, sidewalks, fire lanes, other vehicles, access routes, or neighboring property.

##### 10.9. Parking Violations and Towing

A vehicle may be towed only to the extent permitted by applicable law and HOA authority. Any third-party tow requested by Landlord must comply with applicable notice, signage, police-notification, access, and fee requirements, including OPMC 12.21.030 where applicable. Nothing in this Lease authorizes a tow prohibited by law. Landlord is not responsible for an HOA, city, or other authority's independent lawful towing decision.

##### 10.10. Vehicle Repairs

Vehicle repairs, fluid changes, long-term parking, storage, washing that creates runoff problems, and commercial vehicle activity are prohibited on the Premises or common areas unless Landlord gives written permission and the activity complies with law and HOA rules. Emergency tire changes or battery jumps may be allowed if completed promptly and safely.

##### 10.11. Parking Liability

Landlord does not insure Tenant's vehicles or vehicle contents and does not guarantee against theft, vandalism, weather damage, towing, collision, or other loss. Tenant should maintain appropriate vehicle insurance.

Tenant, occupants, guests, invitees, and animals must comply with lawful HOA rules actually provided to Tenant. Tenant is responsible only to the extent the charge was actually imposed and directly caused by Tenant or a person, animal, or property for whom Tenant is responsible. No markup is added unless expressly stated and lawful.

##### 10.13. HOA Amenities and Pool

Use of any HOA pool, amenity, laundry, parking, or common facility is subject to HOA rules, availability, seasonal closure, maintenance, and suspension. Landlord does not guarantee any amenity unless required by law or expressly stated in writing. Tenant must accompany guests where required and must follow posted rules.

## Article 11 — Move-Out, Abandoned Property, Default, and Remedies

### RLA-460 — Move-Out and Obligation to Vacate

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `11.1`, `11.2`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-460-move-out-and-obligation-to-vacate.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-460-move-out-and-obligation-to-vacate.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard surrender-condition and obligation-to-vacate rules apply at tenancy end?

#### 11.1. Move-Out Condition

At move-out, Tenant must return the Premises clean, empty, undamaged beyond ordinary wear and tear, free of trash and personal property, with all keys/access devices returned, utilities maintained through surrender, and forwarding address provided. Tenant is responsible for cleaning, hauling, repairs, missing items, damages, unpaid amounts, and other lawful charges.

##### 11.2. Obligation to Vacate

If Tenant gives a valid notice to vacate or Landlord gives a valid notice of nonrenewal or termination, Tenant must vacate on or before the stated date unless Landlord gives written consent to remain. Tenant may not unilaterally extend the move-out date.

---

### RLA-470 — Default Events and Notice or Cure

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `11.3`, `11.4`, `11.5`, `11.6`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-470-default-events-and-notice-or-cure.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-470-default-events-and-notice-or-cure.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard material-default, nonpayment, notice, cure, and urgent-lawful-action provisions apply without acceleration or self-help?

#### 11.3. Default Events

A default occurs only when Tenant, an occupant, guest, invitee, animal, or Tenant's property materially fails to comply with a lawful Lease obligation or applicable tenant duty. A minor, technical, disputed, or nonmaterial issue is not automatically a material default. Every remedy remains subject to the notice, cure, service, fair housing, anti-retaliation, and court-process requirements of applicable law.

##### 11.4. Default for Nonpayment

If Base Rent or another amount legally subject to the nonpayment remedy remains unpaid when due, Landlord may deliver a written notice that complies with K.S.A. 58-2564(b) and applicable service law. This Lease does not shorten the required payment period, expand permitted service methods, or authorize filing before the statutory period expires. A disputed fee or reimbursement will not be treated as grounds for an expedited nonpayment eviction unless that remedy is legally available on the established facts.

##### 11.5. Default for Other Breaches

For material noncompliance other than nonpayment, Landlord may deliver a written notice specifying with reasonable factual detail the acts and omissions constituting the breach and stating that this Lease will terminate on a date not less than thirty (30) days after Tenant receives the notice if the breach is not remedied within fourteen (14) days. If Tenant adequately initiates a good-faith cure within the fourteen-day period, the Lease will not terminate on that notice. If the same or a similar breach occurs after the fourteen-day period, Landlord may deliver a second written notice terminating the Lease on a date not less than thirty (30) days after receipt, without another opportunity to cure, only to the extent permitted by K.S.A. 58-2564(a).

##### 11.6. Conduct Requiring Urgent Legal Action

Violence, serious threats, substantial property damage, illegal activity, or another immediate danger may require emergency services, protective orders, injunctive relief, or another lawful expedited response. Nothing in this section creates a contractual immediate eviction or eliminates any notice, cure, service, or court procedure required by law. Landlord may use an expedited or no-cure remedy only when a specific current statute or court order authorizes that remedy on the established facts.

---

### RLA-480 — Abandonment and Property Disposition

- **Clause type:** Personal Property and Abandonment
- **Source sections:** `11.7`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-480-abandonment-and-property-disposition.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-480-abandonment-and-property-disposition.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Are the statutory abandonment facts and the full Kansas storage, publication, mailing, redemption, and disposition process satisfied?

#### 11.7. Abandonment

Landlord may presume abandonment only when the conditions in K.S.A. 58-2565 are satisfied, including that Tenant is at least ten (10) days in default for nonpayment of Base Rent and has removed a substantial portion of Tenant's belongings, unless Tenant has notified Landlord to the contrary. After abandonment, Landlord shall make reasonable efforts to rent the Premises at a fair rental and account for mitigation as required by law.

Personal property remaining after abandonment, surrender, or lawful recovery of possession may be taken and stored at Tenant's expense, but may not be sold or otherwise disposed of until thirty (30) days after Landlord takes possession and completion of the publication and mailing procedure required by K.S.A. 58-2565(d), including publication at least fifteen (15) days before disposition and mailing a copy to Tenant within seven (7) days after publication. Tenant retains the statutory right to redeem before disposition. Nothing in this Lease authorizes earlier disposal.

---

### RLA-490 — Deposit Deductions and Other Charges

- **Clause type:** Deposits and Prepaid Amounts
- **Source sections:** `11.8`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-490-deposit-deductions-and-other-charges.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-490-deposit-deductions-and-other-charges.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Are move-out deductions and any separate charge lawful, documented, and not duplicative?

#### 11.8. Security Deposit Deductions and Other Charges

Landlord may deduct lawful amounts from the Security Deposit and may separately bill Tenant for lawful charges exceeding the deposit. Deductions may include unpaid rent, utilities, cleaning beyond ordinary wear and tear, repairs, damage, missing keys/access devices, hauling, storage, pest treatment caused by Tenant, pet damage, and other legally allowable charges.

### RLA-500 — Remedies, Court Costs, and No Self-Help

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `11.9`, `11.10`, `11.11`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-500-remedies-court-costs-and-no-self-help.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-500-remedies-court-costs-and-no-self-help.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Will only lawful, nonduplicative remedies and court-authorized costs be pursued without self-help eviction?

#### 11.9. Remedies and No Double Recovery

Landlord may pursue lawful remedies including rent, possession, damages, costs, and other relief allowed by law. Landlord will not recover duplicate rent for the same period. Remedies are cumulative only to the extent allowed by law.

##### 11.10. Court Costs, Filing Fees, and Collection Costs

Each party is responsible for that party's attorney fees except when a statute or court order expressly permits an award. Tenant is responsible for filing fees, service fees, sheriff fees, and other court costs only when awarded by a court or otherwise expressly authorized by law. No administrative or collection charge may be used to recover attorney fees prohibited by K.S.A. 58-2547.

##### 11.11. No Self-Help Eviction

Landlord will recover possession only through lawful procedures. Nothing in this Lease authorizes a self-help eviction prohibited by law.

### RLA-510 — Acceptance, Waiver, Collections, and Survival

- **Clause type:** Default, Remedies and Termination
- **Source sections:** `11.12`, `11.13`, `11.14`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-510-acceptance-waiver-collections-and-survival.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-510-acceptance-waiver-collections-and-survival.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard acceptance, reservation, waiver, credit-reporting, collection, and survival provisions apply?

#### 11.12. Acceptance, Reservation, and Waiver

Acceptance of late Base Rent or nonconforming performance has the effect provided by K.S.A. 58-2566. Nothing in this Lease overrides a waiver created by accepting late Base Rent without reservation. Any reservation relating to a particular payment must be made in connection with that payment and comply with applicable law. A delay or one-time exception does not otherwise amend the Lease unless the parties sign a written amendment.

##### 11.13. Credit Reporting and Collections

Landlord may furnish accurate payment history, unpaid balances, damages, judgments, or collection information to lawful recipients. Landlord will use reasonable procedures for accuracy and completeness and will respond to disputes as required by applicable law. Consumer-report information and sensitive records will be retained and disposed of under applicable information-security and disposal requirements.

##### 11.14. Survival

Obligations that by their nature should survive termination or move-out survive only to the extent lawful, including unpaid Base Rent, actual damages, utilities, deposit accounting, lawful notices, confidentiality of access codes, and collection or dispute obligations.

## Article 12 — Insurance, Liability, Notices, Addenda, and Miscellaneous Terms

### RLA-520 — Renter's Insurance and Uninsured Losses

- **Clause type:** Insurance, Risk and Liability
- **Source sections:** `12.1`, `12.2`, `12.3`, `12.4`, `12.5`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-520-renter-s-insurance-and-uninsured-losses.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-520-renter-s-insurance-and-uninsured-losses.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does renter's insurance remain optional and strongly recommended, with no automatic default for declining it?

#### 12.1. Renter's Insurance

Tenant is not required to maintain renter's insurance as a condition of this Lease unless a separate written amendment or addendum signed by Landlord and Tenant states otherwise. Landlord strongly recommends that Tenant obtain and maintain renter's insurance throughout the tenancy, including personal-property coverage, personal-liability coverage, loss-of-use/additional-living-expense coverage, water-damage coverage, theft coverage, fire and smoke coverage, weather-related coverage, vandalism coverage, casualty coverage, and any endorsements Tenant considers appropriate. Tenant may choose the insurance company, coverage limits, deductible, and policy terms. Landlord does not sell insurance, select coverage for Tenant, guarantee that any policy is adequate, or provide insurance advice.

##### 12.2. No Default for Declining Renter's Insurance

Tenant's decision not to maintain renter's insurance is not, by itself, a default. Declining insurance does not limit Tenant's responsibility for Base Rent, lawful Other Charges, actual damage, loss, injury, claims, fines, costs, or liability caused by Tenant, occupants, guests, invitees, ordinary pets, assistance animals, or Tenant's property to the extent allowed by law. Landlord is not required to purchase insurance for Tenant or Tenant's property.

##### 12.3. Tenant Responsibility for Damage and Claims

Tenant is responsible for actual damage, loss, injury, fines, and claims caused by Tenant, occupants, guests, invitees, pets, or Tenant's property to the extent allowed by law. Tenant must promptly notify Landlord of any incident, claim, casualty, injury, police call, fire, flood, or insurance matter involving the Premises.

##### 12.4. Tenant Personal Property and Uninsured Losses

Landlord's insurance does not cover Tenant's personal property, vehicles, stored items, relocation expenses, loss-of-use expenses, or personal liability. If Tenant does not obtain renter's insurance, Tenant accepts the risk that Tenant's losses may be uninsured. Tenant is strongly encouraged to obtain renter's insurance covering theft, fire, smoke, water damage, weather, vandalism, casualty, personal liability, and temporary housing expenses. Nothing in this section waives, reduces, or limits any non-waivable right or remedy Tenant may have for Landlord's breach of a duty imposed by applicable law.

##### 12.5. Insurance and Subrogation

To the extent permitted by law and any applicable insurance policies, each party should look first to available insurance for covered losses. Nothing in this section waives claims that cannot lawfully be waived, requires either party to indemnify the other where prohibited by law, or limits liability in a manner prohibited by Kansas residential landlord-tenant law.

#### 12.6. Subordination, Transfer, and Attornment

This Lease is subordinate to existing and future mortgages, deeds of trust, and security interests only to the extent allowed by law. After written notice of an ownership or management change, Tenant shall recognize a lawful successor and continue Lease performance. Nothing in this section waives or reduces a bona fide tenant's rights under the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act or another applicable foreclosure law.

##### 12.7. Estoppel Certificate

Within ten (10) business days after Landlord's written request, Tenant must sign a reasonable estoppel certificate confirming the Lease status, Rent amount, deposit amount, known defaults, occupants, and other lease facts reasonably requested for sale, financing, refinancing, insurance, or legal compliance. Tenant may identify good-faith disputes in the certificate.

> **Library question:** Is the complete statutory notice information approved, with electronic operational communications not replacing mandatory service methods?

#### 12.8. Notices

All notices must be in writing when the Lease or law requires writing. Statutory default, cure, termination, eviction, protected-person, foreclosure, or other legally prescribed notices shall be delivered by the method and in the format required by the law governing that notice. Email, text, or portal delivery is supplemental unless applicable law and a valid electronic-transactions agreement make electronic delivery sufficient. Notices to Tenant may be addressed to the Premises and any other written notice address Tenant provides.

##### 12.9. Electronic Communications

Tenant consents to reasonable operational communications by email, text, phone, or tenant portal. Consent to sign this Lease electronically does not require either party to conduct every later transaction electronically. Electronic records must remain capable of being downloaded, printed, and retained. Tenant may request a reasonable paper or other nonelectronic communication method or accommodation. This section does not substitute electronic delivery for a statutory service method that remains mandatory.

- **Clause type:** Insurance, Risk and Liability
- **Source sections:** `12.13`, `12.14`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-570-casualty-and-protected-activity.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-570-casualty-and-protected-activity.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Does the standard casualty and force-majeure allocation apply without penalizing lawful protected activity?

#### 12.13. Force Majeure and Casualty

Events beyond a party's reasonable control do not excuse any duty or remedy that applicable law makes non-waivable. If fire or casualty substantially impairs the use and habitability of the Premises, Tenant may vacate immediately and notify Landlord in writing within five (5) days after vacating of Tenant's intention to terminate, in which event the Lease terminates as of the date Tenant vacated. If continued occupancy is lawful, Tenant may vacate the unusable part and Base Rent will be reduced in proportion to the reduction in fair rental value. If the Lease terminates, Landlord shall account for Base Rent as of the vacate date and return the recoverable Security Deposit under K.S.A. 58-2550 and 58-2562.

##### 12.14. False Statements and Protected Activity

Material false statements, fraudulent documents, or material omissions may be a default. Nothing in this Lease penalizes Tenant for exercising lawful rights, making good-faith complaints to government authorities, requesting repairs, requesting fair housing accommodations, or engaging in other protected activity.

### RLA-580 — Data Privacy and Electronic Signatures

- **Clause type:** General Provisions
- **Source sections:** `12.15`, `12.16`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-580-data-privacy-and-electronic-signatures.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-580-data-privacy-and-electronic-signatures.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard lawful data-handling and electronic-signature provisions apply without broader consent or disclosure?

#### 12.15. Data Privacy

Landlord may collect, use, disclose, retain, and destroy Tenant information only for lawful and reasonably necessary housing, payment, maintenance, compliance, collection, financing, sale, and property-management purposes and will use reasonable safeguards appropriate to the information's sensitivity. This Lease is not authorization to disclose consumer reports, bank-account information, identification documents, or disability-related information except as permitted by law. Accommodation and consumer-report records should be maintained separately with restricted access.

##### 12.16. Electronic Signatures and Counterparts

This Lease and any addendum may be signed electronically and in counterparts. Electronic signatures, copies, scans, and PDFs are intended to be enforceable to the same extent as originals under applicable law.

### RLA-590 — Severability, Entire Agreement, and Interpretation

- **Clause type:** General Provisions
- **Source sections:** `12.17`, `12.18`, `12.19`
- **Source JSON:** [`rla-590-severability-entire-agreement-and-interpretation.clause.json`](../../clauses/residential-lease-agreement/rla-590-severability-entire-agreement-and-interpretation.clause.json)
- **Zoho API status:** `tenant_verification_required`

> **Library question:** Do the standard severability, entire-agreement, defined-scope, and interpretation provisions apply?

#### 12.17. Severability

If any provision of this Lease is held invalid or unenforceable, the provision will be limited or reformed to the minimum extent necessary to make it lawful if possible, and the remainder of the Lease will remain enforceable.

##### 12.18. Entire Agreement

This Lease and signed addenda constitute the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant regarding the Premises and supersede prior oral or written statements about the tenancy. Tenant is not relying on any promise, representation, or statement not contained in this Lease or a signed addendum.

##### 12.19. Interpretation

Section headings are for convenience only and do not limit the text. Singular includes plural and plural includes singular where appropriate. Any reference to Tenant includes all Tenants, occupants, guests, invitees, pets, and Tenant's property where context requires. Any rights reserved to Landlord are subject to applicable law.
